Tractional forces from fibrovascular proliferation, retinal breaks, and exudation produce tractional, rhegmatogenous, or exudative retinal detachment.
Contraction of fibrovascular tissue drags the retina into a sickle-shaped falciform fold; the node-level evidence catalogs falciform folds among the tractional sequelae.
Fibrovascular traction drags the optic disc and its emerging vessels (the dragged-disc appearance), the basis of the optic disc abnormalities of advanced FEVR.

Asymmetric loss of central visual input from macular dragging, exudation, or detachment disrupts binocular fusion, producing sensory strabismus; 20% of infants in a large single-gene-positive cohort presented with strabismus at first visit.

nodes.description: The core defect of FEVR. Norrin (NDP) is a secreted ligand that binds the frizzled-4 (FZD4) receptor together with the co-receptor LRP5 and the accessory tetraspanin TSPAN12, activating canonical (beta-catenin-dependent) Wnt signaling specifically in retinal vascular endothelial cells. Loss-of-function in any of these components reduces beta-catenin signaling output. Disruption of Tspan12, Ndp, Fzd4, or Lrp5 in mice produces similar ocular phenotypes, indicating a shared signaling pathway.

evidence.snippet: Gene disruptions of Tspan12 (Junge et al., 2009), Ndp (Luhmann et al., 2005), Fzd4 (Xu et al., 2004; Ye et al., 2009), and Lrp5 (Xia et al., 2008) all result in similar ocular phenotypes in mice, characterized by defects in intraretinal capillary development and dysregulation of the blood-retina barrier.

nodes.description: Norrin/Wnt signaling in retinal endothelial cells governs not only developmental angiogenesis but also formation and maintenance of the inner blood-retinal barrier (iBRB). Loss-of-function in FZD4, LRP5, NDP, or TSPAN12 impairs iBRB integrity, producing aberrant vascular permeability that contributes to retinal exudation independently of ischemia-driven neovascularization. FEVR, Norrie disease, and persistent fetal vascular syndrome share this iBRB dysfunction as a unifying pathophysiological element.

nodes.description: KIF11 encodes EG5, a homotetrameric kinesin required for bipolar mitotic spindle assembly. Heterozygous KIF11 mutations impair spindle formation in proliferating progenitors, compromising CNS growth (microcephaly) and the development of retinal and lymphatic structures. This mechanism operates outside the canonical Norrin/Wnt pathway and defines the KIF11-related FEVR spectrum (microcephaly-lymphedema-chorioretinal dysplasia).
